design.product: StaticModuleProduct: exact SCM/profile/generator/module identities, generated C and link-info digests, ModuleSpec/FrameSpec ABI and publication receipt
design.producer: Expose per-module target generation as independent existing compile jobs with private output. Publish C and link metadata together only after complete success; preserve original feature/options/module naming.
design.consumer: LinkPlan consumes the original ordered module set of sealed target/link-info products. Missing or stale products schedule their producer, never an implicit serial SCM recompile inside the linker.
design.invalidation: SCM, macro/include, generator, module mode/naming, target/profile or ABI change invalidates affected products and downstream LinkPlan; link-order-only change retains qualified module products.
design.retirement: Retire raw SCM list at build-bach link only after target equivalence, ordered linking, roots/frame/module identities, failure custody, original compiler and both packages pass.
design.cost: Fresh cold target generation remains; parallelism adds process/context setup and publication overhead. Warm hits may remove generation only with exact producer identity. Dynamic runtime C is not assumed equivalent to static C.

proofRouting.qnt: Reuse existing native artifact partition/publication models for producer ownership, joins, late/unknown completion and link admission; concrete42-module refinement OPEN.
proofRouting.lean: Target/link-info equivalence, original ordered-link result and FrameSpec/ModuleSpec fidelity, plus critical-span/net-removal inequalities; OPEN. Do not duplicate QNT histories.

implementation.role: Existing capability owns native processes, content identities, durable completion and bounded phase joins; Gerbil declares original module/argv order.
implementation.actualTarget: Preserve canonical static C basename, track-scheme, SMP/include arguments and original native object/link order.
implementation.reuse: C products keyed by source bytes/path, effective generation argv and closed provider identity; LinkPlan keyed by ordered metadata/path identities and provider. Durable source-bound completion plus byte digests required on each hit.
implementation.objectReuse: Disabled: native include closure is not sealed. All native objects are rebuilt, no C-hash-only admission.
implementation.invalidationLimit: Provider conservatively includes plan-producer and framework file digests: edits to these files invalidate all C products, even if they only change planning. Runtime source-only plan reordering under an unchanged provider retains products. Finer source-proof factoring is OPEN.

currentWarmInventory.scope: Exact retained SCM bytes under unchanged provider. Does not include Scheme regeneration, object compilation or whole-stage reuse.

phaseCosts.warning: Spans include overlapping parallel actions; process seconds must not be added as wall time. No matched serial42 timing or package speedup.

sourceRefinementGaps.restamping: compiler/driver.ss:27 creates current-time compile timestamp; base.ss:204 uses it in quoted gensym identity. Exact byte reuse cannot silently remove or normalize this value. A whole prepared source product needs dependency/context proof before reuse.
sourceRefinementGaps.stdlibObservations: Stdlib timeout stdout reports334 compile actions and739 compile-job starts. These are starts, not completed products or durations; no per-job completion receipt, so partial file presence cannot qualify outputs.
sourceRefinementGaps.packageRouting: StaticModuleProduct is currently the BACH compiler pipeline; default package gxc producers are not yet consumers of the new service.
sourceRefinementGaps.referenceComparison: Existing earlier42 inventory:3 exact SCM/C matches, main SCM absent; a real runtime/util diff contains timestamp change. Not a42-module semantic equivalence proof.
sourceRefinementGaps.coldNetGain: No matched serial baseline for this source/profile. Cold stage still creates42 C files and43 objects; twofold package claim remains unestablished.
